task: Build an independent ground-truth test fixture for poker hand evaluation, completely separate from wherever poker_ai is being vendored (use a different directory, e.g. tests/ground_truth/, so this does not collide with that other in-progress task). Per this repo's CLAUDE.md rule, hand evaluation must come from real, separately-maintained code, never logic written by an AI -- so pick a well-established, widely-used Python poker hand-evaluation library (e.g. treys or deuces; verify it's real and maintained, don't guess) and add it as a proper dependency. Using that library, write automated tests for a handful of known hands/boards with unambiguous correct answers (at minimum: royal flush beats full house, two pair beats a straight [i.e. loses to it -- get the direction right], and at least one genuinely close comparison like two-pair-vs-two-pair with different kickers). Each test should assert the library's real output matches the known-correct ranking. This is meant as a durable sanity check we'll keep using later to validate whatever hand-evaluation code the final bot actually uses.
done_when: the test fixture is committed, uses a real named external library (not hand-written logic), and running it (record the exact command) passes on this machine right now, independent of whether poker_ai vendoring has finished
